reviews.reason: Develop a general mechanical food-processing operation through the current-conversation handoff. Related capabilities have been searched. probe supports observation and a consumptive press test, but its documented modes do not implement peeling, cutting, shell fracture or conserved processing products. The existing hazelnut press finding establishes only that a 0.2 load was held without flexibility, not that the shell can be opened. unheated-food-preparation only dry-brushes whole units; it is not equivalent. The retrieved candidates are incomplete, so absence of any other equivalent is not established: the handoff must check the remaining related registry contracts before adding code and use any equivalent implementation and its existing learning duration instead. Missing physical mechanisms warrant development, not permanent rejection or a claim that these particular foods can already be processed.

reviews.specification:
General operation: Mechanical food separation. Parameters: exact owned inputStackId, quantity in supported inventory increments, mode inspect or trial, operation open/peel/cut, optional exact implementId and supportId, and progress/resume/cancel modes. Any applicable actor may learn it. Implement the smallest supported hands-on separation trial, not tool manufacture, cooking or a sequence of future unlocks. Reuse existing ownership, reach, inventory splitting, ageing, observations and event machinery, recording exact reused handlers and revisions; record probe/open.probe/foundation-open@1 as an existing comparison, not a newly invented press test. Do not assume its press output implements fracture.
Current references: lin owns item-180-lin-2343, quantity 2 roots, and item-19-lin-197, quantity 0.9 hazelnut. Recheck their live condition and location; old inspection records are not current safety tests. No implement, water, fire, vessel or suitable support has been established. Source plants are not owned supplies. Do not spawn equipment, replacement food or knowledge. Do not round 0.9 hazelnut into a whole nut or infer its geometry from the resource name; determine whether that remainder has represented processable structure. Whole-shell opening requires an actual intact shell; a suitable fragment may instead support an applicable separation trial.
Handoff must supply an executable material/contact kernel before activation: represented geometry, accessible edges/layers or shell, grip/support requirements, bounded hand or implement force and work, separation/fracture resistance, and product allocation. Use authoritative implementation properties without disclosing hidden values to the actor. Do not derive these properties or edibility from names or arbitrary success rolls. If the needed properties are absent, implement their minimal supported representation in this handoff, explicitly documenting model assumptions and provenance rather than calling them discoveries. Until a separation rule is supported, the executable precursor is an observation or bounded contact attempt reporting unknown/not established, never a successful opening. A cutting action requires an actually acquired suitable edge and support; hand peeling requires a represented accessible separable layer; hand opening requires a represented shell and force within hand capacity. No teeth-based ingestion, forced injury or automatic equipment acquisition.
Costs: proposed study 3 rounds at 0.2 energy each, individually paid by each learner. inspect or inspect-progress costs 1 round and 0.2 energy, using no food. A supported trial consists of one setup round at 0.2 energy and one bounded working round at 0.5 energy; quantity selects at most one processable unit or represented fragment per bout. The kernel must publish its force/work limit and implement wear or breakage costs before execution. Unsupported modes, missing ownership/reach/means, invalid quantities and insufficient energy refuse before charging; an actual paid observation/contact that finds uncertainty or resistance remains a completed observation/contact, not a processing success. No arbitrary mandatory food destruction: loss occurs only through modeled separation, damage, spillage or wear. Additional bouts require fresh checks and their own costs.
Setup reserves the selected quantity without copying or consuming it. Store exact item/version, quantity, chosen operation, means, completed paid phase and any actual partial damage. Each working phase atomically debits the input portion and creates only physically supported products: retained food portions, detached peel/shell, fragments and accounted unrecoverable debris, with explicit conversion and a material ledger. Total material cannot increase; implement loss must also be accounted for. If the inventory cannot represent these outputs, extend it minimally before enabling separation rather than rounding or creating stock. Preserve origin, age, decay, contamination and unknown safety; distribute existing nutritional contents without multiplying them. Do not count shell or peel as edible merely because its parent stack was food. Failed contact may leave the input unchanged or actually damaged as the kernel determines. No identification, detoxification, improved nutrition, preservation, safety certification or feeding follows from this action.
Another action, loss of reach, low energy or unavailable means pauses before further charges; resume revalidates the exact input, current damage and means and performs only unpaid work. Changed or missing inputs invalidate outstanding reservations. Cancel costs one round and no energy, releases unchanged reserved material once and retains all real products, damage and expenditure. Death stops work, clears reservations once and leaves material/products under ordinary death and ownership rules. No time, energy, lost material or wear refunds; no undo of completed changes. Products continue ordinary ageing; there is no autonomous processing, special maintenance or passive benefit. Inspection never freezes decay. Work and study advance time only on actual paid simulation actions; review/development waiting does not. All eligibility, charging, conservation, progress and outcome rules execute in code, not repeated model adjudication.

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
candidates.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.2 energy each. inspect: targetIds 1-4 of your items; 1 round, 0.2; reserves and uses nothing. trial: targetIds [rubbing piece, base piece], whole units (one id twice needs 2 units), quantity 1, effortRounds 1-10 (default 3): a paid inspection round (0.2) unless you inspected those unchanged pieces within 10 rounds, then 0.8 energy per rubbing round (a round an ember stops pays only the rubbing done). trial again on open work starts a new bout after fresh checks; resume continues a paused bout; inspect-progress: 1 round, 0.2; cancel: 1 round, no energy. Refusals come before any cost. No tool, tinder or fuel is given.
candidates.effects: Pieces: branch, birch or oak units as the small-combustion-source@1 rod (900 kg/m3, 25 diameters long, rigid); rubbing piece 1.5-5 cm thick, base 3 cm+, both 0.3 m+; the base is braced on clear firm ground beside you. Model (1 energy = 21.6 kJ): 50 N press, friction 0.4, stroke min(0.25 m, base/2) at 2 cycles/s: 20 W for up to 864 s a round. A share 0.5+track mm/3 (max 1) heats a 6 J/K spot, the rest two 50 g zones; losses: 0.012 W/K into each zone, convection 10 W/m2K on 4 cm2 x (1+0.5 wind), radiation (emissivity 0.9), zone convection on 100 cm2, and water the wood draws (1.9e-5 kg/s x water share) boiling off above 100 C. Wear: 2 g per 21.6 kJ, split inversely by hardness, debited from the pieces; dry solids become dust; the 1 cm base track ends the work half through the base. Dust of 2 g+ at 350 C+, rain 0.15 or less, becomes one ember: 18 MJ/kg, burning dust x dt/(600 s/(1+wind)), 10% ash, glowing until below 300 C, burned out or rain above 0.15; standing on it costs 5 health per 2 MJ released. Contacts cool every round; resume keeps the cooled state. Another action, lost site, unsafe effort (health under 20, starving, body outside 7-34 C) or low energy pauses free; changed pieces end it; cancel or death ends it, releases the pieces once and leaves dust and any ember. No flame, tinder, food heating, warmth, refund or reward.

candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds. Every round is checked before any charge; prepare resumes your paused work (inputStackId and quantity may be omitted). Inspect (inputStackId of your own food) and inspect-progress (your latest preparation): one round, 0.2 energy, no food used. Cancel: one round, no energy. No vessel, water, fuel, tool or ground surface is used or given. Eating and giving use eat and give at their own costs.
candidates.effects: Each paid round separates one whole unit from the input, checks it by eye and brushes it by hand, held, never set on the ground. A usable unit joins one owned lot of the same food with unchanged quantity, origin, age, decay, nutrition and toxicity, recorded as raw, unheated, dry-brushed, safety unknown. Loose soil on food is not represented, so no debris is measured or removed and no cleanliness is claimed. A spoiled unit is reported unsuitable, stays unprepared and ends the work. Nothing is cooked, peeled, washed, made safe or kept fresher; food keeps ageing, and the planting trial treats prepared units as processed. The lot holds only completed units. Inspections record visible condition, treatment and your own eating record (not a safety test) as an unverified personal record. An unworked round, too little energy, or an input no longer yours with a whole unit pauses without charge. Cancel or death ends the work; completed units stay. No refund or reward; nobody is fed.

candidates.costs: Study: 1 round, 0.2 energy. inspect: target (your carried item), optional x, y and angle (radians); 1 round, 0.2 energy; reports the unit and site facts. place: target, x, y, angle, quantity 1 (one unit at a time). Round 1 is the same paid inspection (0.2) and reserves the unit, still carried; round 2 moves and orients it through ordinary drop (0.5): 2 rounds, 0.7 energy in all. inspect-progress: 1 round, 0.2. resume continues the unpaid round 2 after fresh checks; cancel: 1 round, no energy; both use only mode. Refusals come before any cost; travel and pickup cost separately.
candidates.effects: Needs a represented shape: branch, birch and oak units are the declared rod of small-combustion-source@1 (900 kg/m3, length 25 diameters; a branch is about 0.04 x 0.99 m), straight and rigid. Other materials, bending willow, worked, combined or partial units are reported as unknown shape and cannot be placed. Handling: a unit you carry whose rod fits a two-handed grip (1.5-5 cm thick). Site: the centre within your reach (body radius + 0.65), the whole footprint inside the world, on firm visible ground (not water, a wet bank or waterlogged), clear of people (you included), objects, placed units and loose ground items. Placing debits exactly that unit and lays it, with its material, origin and age, as one ground item (the new id that drop gives, mapped) at x, y and the angle, plus a footprint record others see; nothing is copied, merged, shaped, joined or fastened. Another action, an obstruction, lost reach or low energy pauses before round 2 without charge; a changed unit or ground ends the work (place again). Cancel or death releases the unit once; nothing is refunded. Recover it with pickup; the footprint record ends when the item is taken or moved. No reward, comfort or skill gain.
